8

Q.        What is the purpose of the Panel’s corrections and updates testimony? 
11 
A.     The Panel’s testimony explains and supports certain corrections and updates 
12 
to KEDNY’s April 30, 2019 base rate filing (“April 30 filing”) in this 
13 
proceeding. 
14 
 
15 
Q. 
Does the corrections and updates testimony also address the June 11, 
16 
2019 supplemental filing?   
17 
A. 
No.  The supplemental filing was made to illustrate the potential impacts to 
18 
the April 30 filing if KEDNY is unable to obtain incremental natural gas 
19 
supplies from the NESE project.  At this time, the Company remains 
20 
optimistic that the NESE project will be approved.  Therefore, all corrections 
21

Q. 
Please explain how the corrections and updates are organized. 
1 
A. 
The exhibits submitted in this filing show corrections and/or updates and 
2 
indicate the change from the original filing.  The exhibits are labeled with 
3 
“CU” after the original label.  For example, Exhibit __ (RRP-1) in the April 
4 
30 filing is the Statement of Operating Income.  The exhibit showing the 
5 
corrections and/or updates to the Statement of Operating Income is labeled 
6 
Exhibit ___ (RRP-1CU).  The first page of each exhibit provides a summary 
7 
of all adjustments made and reflected in that exhibit.  This summary, or lead 
8 
page, is identified as “Corrections and Updates” under each exhibit number.  
9 
The revised schedules and pages supporting each exhibit correspond to the 
10 
schedules and pages originally filed.  The Company has only included 
11 
exhibits, summaries, schedules, and pages where corrections and/or updates 
12 
were made.   
13 
 
14 
The information requests referenced in the Panel’s testimony are included in 
15 
the workpapers in Exhibit ___ (RRP-11CU) and correspond to the specific 
16 
exhibits and schedules where the corrections and/or updates were made.  For 
17 
example, if a correction and/or update is shown in Exhibit ___ (RRP-3CU), 
18 
Schedule 2 based on a response to an information request, that information 
19 
request is included in the workpapers supporting Exhibit ___ (RRP-3CU), 
20 


--- Page 6 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 4 of 27 
 
Schedule 2.  Where the attachments to information requests are voluminous, 
1 
the Company included only the written response and relevant attachments.   
2 
 
3 
Q. 
What impact do the corrections and updates have on KEDNY’s revenue 
4 
requirement in this proceeding? 
5 
A. 
The April 30 filing reflected a Rate Year revenue requirement that was $236.8 
6 
million greater than revenue at present rates.  The corrections and updates 
7 
decrease the Company’s revenue requirement for the Rate Year by $41.1 
8 
million, to $195.6 million, as shown in Exhibit ___ (RRP-1CU), Page 2, and 
9 
the table below. 
10 
Rate Year 
April 30th 
Filing 
Corrections & 
Updates 
Increase/ 
(Decrease) 
KEDNY 
$237m 
$196m 
($41m) 
 
11 
Q. 
What are the primary drivers of the decrease to the revenue requirement 
12 
in the Rate Year? 
13 
A. 
The primary drivers of the decrease to the revenue requirement in the Rate 
14 
Year are (i) an update to the Company’s revenue forecast that increased gas 
15 
sales revenues, (ii) updates and corrections that decreased KEDNY’s capital 
16 
forecast and (iii) corrections that collectively reduced the Company’s O&M 
17 
expense. 
18

Schedule 1 – Consultant Expense 
12 
Schedule 1 reflects two adjustments to consultant expense.  The first 
13

Schedule 2 – Contractor Expense 
20 
Schedule 2 reflects eight adjustments to contractor expense.   
21 


--- Page 9 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 7 of 27 
 
The first four adjustments were made for presentation purposes to reclassify 
1 
paving expense from Schedule 2 to Schedule 40 (paving).  The purpose of the 
2 
change is to provide all paving-related costs in one schedule.  There is no 
3 
revenue requirement impact from the re-classifications, which are discussed in 
4 
the Company’s response to Information Request No. DPS-236 Supplemental.   
5 
 
6 
The fifth adjustment was made to reclassify an accrual from contractors to 
7 
other expense.  In the April 30 filing, the Company made a normalization 
8 
adjustment to contractor expense.  However, the adjustment related to an 
9 
accrual that was booked to other expense.  This adjustment corrects the error 
10 
by re-classifying the normalization to other expense.   
11 
 
12 
The sixth adjustment pertains to a normalization adjustment to disconnect and 
13 
reconnect expense that the Company inadvertently made to the Rate Year in 
14 
the April 30 filing, that should have been made instead to the Historic Test 
15 
Year.  The correction moves the adjustment from the Rate Year to the Historic 
16 
Test Year and includes the change in inflation. 
17 
 
18 
The seventh adjustment was made to reflect the update to the Local Law 30 
19 
forecast and correct the normalization adjustment made to the Rate Year that 
20 
should have been made instead to the Historic Test Year.   
21

VI. 
Federal and State Income Taxes 
1 
Q. 
Has the Company made any corrections or updates to federal and state 
2 
income tax expense? 
3 
A. 
Yes, the Company made adjustments to reflect changes to the amortization of 
4 
excess accumulated deferred income tax (“ADIT”) and to reflect the flow 
5 
through effect of changes in rate base on income tax expense, as shown in 
6 
Exhibit ___ (RRP-6CU). 
7 
 
8 
Q. 
Please describe the change to the amortization of excess ADIT. 
9 
A. 
The Company rolled forward the overall excess ADIT amount from December 
10 
2018 to March 2019 to match the plant roll forward balance and to reflect 
11 
adjustments to income tax reserves that were due to the settlement of the 
12 
August 24, 2007 to March 31, 2009 federal income tax audit.  For the audit 
13 
adjustments that were temporary, the current income tax was booked at 35 
14 
percent, the deferred tax was booked at 21 percent, and the difference 
15 
increased or decreased the regulatory liability for excess ADIT.  The 
16 
amortization lives were applied to the adjusted numbers, resulting in changed 
17 
total excess ADIT amortization amounts. 
18 
 
19 
 
20 
 
21

Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 20 of 27

Rate Base 
1

3

4 
of a lead Corrections and Updates page, a Summary with four pages, and six 
5

6 
assets and liabilities (Schedule 2), federal and state accumulated deferred 
7 
income taxes (Schedule 3), working capital (Schedule 4), the lead lag study 
8 
(Schedule 5), and City/State Construction Accounts Receivable (Schedule 7).

A. 
Forecast of Net Utility Plant In Service 
11 
Q. 
Please describe the changes made to the forecast of average net utility 
12 
plant, as shown in Exhibit ___ (RRP-7CU), Schedule 1.   
13 
A. 
Schedule 1 reflects three adjustments.  The first adjustment reflects updates to 
14

15 
to use the actual March 31, 2019 construction work in progress, plant in 
16 
service, depreciation reserve, and retirement work in progress beginning 
17 
balances.  The Company also updated the composite depreciation rates using 
18 
depreciable plant balances as of March 2019.

Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel

The second adjustment updates the Company’s capital forecast. The 
1 
adjustment was made to update the capital and cost of removal forecasts for 
2 
certain projects presented in Exhibit ___ (GIOP-1CU) for direct capital 
3 
expenditures and Exhibit ___ (GIOP-7CU) for indirect capital expenditures.  
4 
The corrections and update testimony of the GIOP discusses the specific 
5 
adjustments in more detail. 
6 
 
7 
The third adjustment updates the gas plant forecast to incorporate revised in-
8

9

B. 
Deferred Taxes 
12 
Q. 
Please describe the changes made to the deferred tax forecasts, as shown 
13 
in Exhibit ___ (RRP-7CU), Schedule 3. 
14 
A. 
The Company made changes to rate base ADIT to (i) flow through the impact 
15 
of the return of excess ADIT, (ii) add the impact of taking bonus depreciation 
16 
on the fiscal year end March 31, 2019 federal income tax return, (iii) update 
17 
ADIT balances from December 2018 to March 2019, and (iv) flow through 
18 
the rate base ADIT impact of changes to book plant additions, cost of 
19 
removal, and book depreciation. 
20 
 
21 


--- Page 24 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 22 of 27 
 
Q. 
How does the change in excess ADIT amortization effect rate base? 
1 
A. 
As the Company returns excess ADIT, the excess ADIT regulatory liability 
2 
that is included in rate base decreases and rate base is correspondingly 
3 
increased.  Rate base ADIT adjustments were made to reflect the updated 
4 
amortization amounts that flow through cost of service.  Also, the Company 
5 
determined that in the April 30 filing, the rate base adjustment included the 
6 
excess ADIT related to both National Grid USA Service Company and 
7 
KEDNY.  Accordingly, the Company updated the rate base formula to include 
8 
only the amortization related to KEDNY. 
9 
 
10 
Q. 
How did bonus depreciation change rate base ADIT?  
11 
A. 
After additional analysis and conversations with industry experts and other 
12 
industry peers, the Company determined it would deduct additional bonus 
13 
depreciation in accordance with the pre-tax reform regulations.  Bonus 
14 
depreciation will be 40 percent for those assets started before September 28, 
15 
2017 and placed in service between April 1, 2018 and December 31, 2018.  
16 
Bonus depreciation of 30 percent will be taken on assets started before 
17 
September 28, 2017 and placed in service between January 1 and March 31, 
18 
2019.   
19 
 
20

Response: 
 
1.
a.
The Historic Test Year reflects costs of $0.071 million for KEDNY and $0.043 
million for KEDLI related to the management and operations audit in Case 18-M-
0195 (“Management Audit”).   
b. No adjustment was made to reflect Rate Year costs for the Management Audit.  As 
such, the costs embedded in the Rate Year are equivalent to the Historic Test Year 
costs plus general inflation.   
In preparing this response, the Company realized the above costs should be 
normalized and replaced with KEDNY and KEDLI’s allocable share of the $1.988 
million compensation limit set forth in the audit contract in the Management Audit.  
In corrections and updates, KEDNY and KEDLI will remove the amount included in 
the Historic Test Year and replace with the amortized portion of KEDNY and 
KEDLI’s allocable share of the Management Audit contract costs.     
2.
a-d. There are no costs or savings associated with implementation of recommendations in 
Case 13-G-0009 (Gas Management Audit), Case 13-M-0314 (“Data Audit”), or Case 
13-M-0449 (“Staffing Audit”) in the Historic Test Year or Rate Year, as the 
recommendations were implemented prior to the Historic Test Year and/or did not 
involve any incremental costs.  Benefits were qualitative in nature with no savings 
identified in the Rate Year.  
e.  The Management Audit is ongoing with a final report scheduled for September 
2019.  As such, any potential costs or savings are unknown at the moment.

“The Company is proposing to remove the 50-foot threshold and capitalize all main 
installation activities in accordance with the FERC Chart of Accounts –Gas – Operating 
Expense Instructions, Accounts Mains and 376 Mains. This change will standardize the 
accounting treatment of these work activities between National Grid’s New York gas 
distribution companies. As discussed in the testimony of the Revenue Requirements 
Panel, the Company has normalized its Historic Test Year (HTY) to reflect the change 
from expense to capital for distribution and transmission main installation, and the 
Company’s capital investment forecasts also reflect this capitalization change.”

of main under 50-feet, incurred during the HTY.

account for the proposed accounting change.

a.

feet during the HTY was $688,858, as presented on Exhibit RRP-11, Workpapers to 
Exhibit RRP-3, Schedule 2, Workpaper 4.

removes a set amount of leak repair cost calculated by taking the number of incremental
leak repairs associated with lowering the type 3 leak backlog, 205 leak repairs in
Calendar Year 2018, multiplied by the average unit cost of a leak repair which is equal to
$4,596.

1. 
KEDNY provided an Other Expenses amount by Provider Company (including “Keyspan

Service Company and All Other Companies”) for the Historic Test Year (HTY) in the 
Exhibit___(RRP-3), OM Schedule 7 Other, Tab, “Page 1” that are different than the 
amounts provided in the  Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpapers to RRP-3, Schedule 7, WP 1, 
Tab “Summary” explain the difference in the HTY amount for each Provider Company. 
2. 
Referencing to Exhibit___(RRP-3), OM Schedule 7 Other, Tab, “Page 5,” Cell, “H56” 
the exhibit shows Adjustments of $2,890.2.  Whereas, Exhibit___(RRP-3), OM Schedule 
7 Other, Tab, “Page 1,” Cell, shows the Adjustments to Normalize Historic Test Year of 
“2,659.7.”  Explain the differences and reconcile the differences between the amounts. 
Response: 
 
1.
The amounts listed for each Provider Company on Exhibit___(RRP-3), Schedule 7, Page 
1 were developed immediately following the closing of the Company’s books to populate 
the historic test year data.  Upon subsequently running a new report to break out the 
individual lines of accounting by component for Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpapers to 
RRP-3, Schedule 7, Workpaper 1, the accounting data was further delineated to break out 
costs by provider company.  As noted, the total amount did not change.  The resulting 
difference is a presentation issue; however, the end result is the same.   
2.
The formula on Exhibit___(RRP-3), Schedule 7, Page 1 by Provider Company 
inadvertently excluded Rows 19 and 20 of Exhibit___(RRP-3), Schedule 7, Page 5, 
Exhibit____(RRP-3CU)

resulting in a difference of $0.230 million.  However, the formula on Page 1 to break out 
by FERC category was correctly linked to Page 5 and this is the amount that is used to 
calculate total O&M expense.  Therefore, this does not impact the revenue requirement.  
The Company will correct the formula for adjustments by Provider Company in the 
Corrections and Updates filing.

SUBJECT:
Other Expenses (FL Accrual)- KEDNY 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
Referring to the MS Excel File, “Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpapers to Exhibit___(RRP-3), 
Schedule 7, WP 1,” explain what each CO Documents type of FL Accrual item listed below is 
and explain why KEDNY includes these amounts in other expenses. 
1.
159414175 of $12.55 million; 
2.
WAN Invoice Allocations of $0.92 million; 
3.
Appreciate Award Dec FY19 of $0.49 million; and 
4.
Accrue Travel Expense of $0.04 million. 
Response: 
 
1.
The purpose of this entry is to post an accrual related to City State Construction charges 
included in the deferred expense account that are in excess of the amounts billable under 
existing reimbursement agreements.  Charges to the deferred expense account for 
disconnect/reconnect and watch guard work are billed to the City at an agreed upon rate 
and amounts above that are posted to expense.  This accrual is an estimate of the amounts 
that should be posted to expense based on what has historically been invoiced.  The 
accrual represents charges for active projects that will be billed at the completion of the 
project.  
Exhibit____(RRP-3CU)
Schedule 7
Workpaper 5
Page 3 of 4


--- Page 433 ---
Form 103 
2.
This amount represents the December 2018 accrual for network service and telecom 
vendors that have provided services for the month that have not been billed.  The accruals 
are booked to other expense and reversed the following month. 
3.
This entry was to record the December 2018 accrual for the unbilled appreciate program 
costs.  In addition, other expense in the historic test year includes the reversal of the prior 
year’s accruals, resulting in a net amount related to appreciate program costs in other 
expense of $0.07 million.   
As described in the testimony of the Revenue Requirement Panel and shown on 
Exhibit__(RRP-3), Schedule 1, Workpaper 3, the Company removed from the Historic 
Test Year the vendor costs associated with the appreciate program.  The Company 
inadvertently excluded the historic test year net accrual amount in other expense from the 
adjustment.  The Company will remove the $0.07 million in its Corrections and Updates 
filing.  KEDLI will also remove the $(.01) million from its other expense in Corrections 
and Updates filing.   
4.
The purpose of this entry is to accrue travel card transactions that have not posted to the 
books as of December 2018.  The accrual is booked to other expense and reversed the 
following month.  The actuals will subsequently be posted to the actual lines of 
accounting.

years 2016-2018, and to date 2019. Include a detailed explanation for any delays or 
unscheduled interruptions to the program.

2.
The project commenced in November 2018 and the project schedule is included in 
Section 1.14 (Key Milestones) of the sanction paper.  The Company maintains a Portfolio 
tracking report but there is no separate spreadsheet in MS Excel File Format that tracks

Date of Request:  May 30, 2019

Due Date:  June 10, 2019 
NG Request No. NG-351
KEYSPAN GAS EAST CORPORATION d/b/a NATIONAL GRID 
THE BROOKLYN UNION GAS COMPANY d/b/a NATIONAL GRID NY 
Case Nos. 19-G-0309 & 19-G-0310 
Gas Utilities Rates 
Request for Information 
FROM: 
DPS Staff, John Castano 
TO: 
National Grid, Revenue Requirements Panel (KEDNY) 
SUBJECT:
Labor - Capitalization 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
1.
On a monthly and on-going basis, provide an updated 12-month average of KEDNY’s
actual labor costs, broken down between expense, capital, and other, beginning January
2019.
2.
As stated on p.63, ln 3 of KEDNY’s Revenue Requirements Panel testimony, “The
Company forecast 50.53 percent of total labor costs would be capitalized in the Rate Year
(RY). The forecast is based on the Historic Test Year (HTY) percentage of labor costs
capitalized.”
a.
Does KEDNY anticipate a greater level of capital work to be performed during
the RY? If yes, explain why the Company believes the amount of labor costs
capitalized in the HTY, is indicative of the amount of labor costs to be capitalized
in the RY.
b.
For KEDNY, provide the dollar amount of capital work performed during the
HTY.
c.
For KEDNY, provide the dollar amount of capital work to be performed during
the RY.
d.
For KEDNY, provide the dollar amount of capital work performed for Calendar
Years (CY) 2016, and 2017.
e.
For KEDNY, provide the percent of total labor costs capitalized for CY 2016, and
2017.
Exhibit______(RRP-11CU)
Workpapers to Exhibit (RRP-5CU) 
Schedule 23
Workpaper 16
Page 1 of 5


--- Page 662 ---
Form 103 
3. 
As stated on p. 62, ln 9 of KEDNY’s Revenue Requirements Panel testimony, “[w]ith 
respect to KEDNY, the Company made adjustments to: (i) reflect changes to the 
capitalization policy to remove the 50-foot threshold and capitalize all main installation 
activities…” Explain whether KEDNY accounted for this change when determining the 
HTY percentage of labor costs capitalized. If yes, provide the supporting calculation. If 
not, explain why not, and provide an updated calculation including this change. 
Response: 
 
1.   
Please see Attachment 1 for the rolling 12-month average of KEDNY’s originating 
company labor costs, broken down between operating expense, non-operating expense, 
capital and other, beginning January 2019. 
2a.  
Yes, the Company anticipates a greater level of capital work to be performed during the 
Rate Year.  However, an increase in capital work does not warrant an adjustment to the 
Rate Year labor capitalization rate.  The Company’s labor expense forecast follows 
Historic Test Year (“HTY”) accounting.  Specifically, the labor model applies the HTY 
capitalization ratio to a total labor amount that is calculated based on headcount at the 
end of the HTY.  The Company’s level of O&M expense work in the HTY will not 
decrease in the Rate Year because of more capital work.  Indeed, the same base level of 
O&M expense work is projected to continue in the Rate Year.  Therefore, applying an 
HTY capitalization ratio is appropriate.   
With respect to the projected increase in capital work, that work will be supported 
through the addition of the proposed FTEs set forth in Exhibit ___ (RRP-3), Schedule 27 
(Other Initiatives).  These incremental FTEs receive an 85 to 90 percent allocation to 
capital labor.     
Importantly, use of the HTY capitalization rate to forecast Rate Year labor expense has 
been used to set rates in National Grid’s most recent rate case proceedings (see Cases 16-
G-0058 and 16-G-0059 and Cases 17-E-0238 and 17-G-0239).  If the labor capitalization 
rate were adjusted, an adjustment would need to be made to increase contractor expense 
to cover the O&M expense work performed in the HTY that will continue in the Rate 
Year.   
2b.  
Please see Exhibit __ (RRP-3), Schedule 23, Page 9 for the amount of capital labor

KEDNY’s adjustment to the HTY was a reduction of $539,068 to KEDNY’s originating 
company labor expense and an increase to capital labor.  In reviewing the adjustment, it 
was determined that the adjustment should have been $533,220 to KEDNY originating 
company labor costs and $4,425 to Service Company originating company labor costs.  
In addition, the Company inadvertently did not include the adjustment to the HTY for 
variable pay related to the capitalization change (KEDNY originating company of 
$16,369 and Service Company originating of $330).  The Company will include these 
adjustments in its Corrections & Updates filing.

Referring to pp.34-35 Maureen Heaphy’s testimony, it states “[p]ursuant to their respective 
union contracts, members of TWU Local 101 (KEDNY) will receive a base wage increase of 1.5 
percent on April 16, 2019; members of IBEW Local 3 (KEDNY) will receive a base wage 
increase of 1.5 percent on April 16, 2019, October 16, 2019 and April 16, 2020; and members of 
IBEW Local 1049 (KEDLI) received a base wage increase of 3.0 percent on February 14, 2019 
and will receive 3.0 percent on February 14, 2020. These base wage increases are also set forth 
in Schedule 1 of Exhibit __(MPH-4). Because all of these collective bargaining agreements are 
scheduled to expire during the course of these rate proceedings (the TWU Local 101 contract 
expires on October 15, 2019, the IBEW Local 3 contract expires on October 15, 2020 and the 
IBEW Local 1049 contract expires on February 13, 2021), the Companies have included 
projected base pay increases in the revenue requirements, assuming new contracts are negotiated 
upon the expiration of the existing contracts. These projections are not intended to guarantee that 
increases will be included in the contract negotiations.” 
1.
For KEDNY, provide the latest union contracts supporting the associated wage increases. 
2.
For KEDNY, referring to the Excel file for Exhibit___(RRP-3), OM Schedule 23, WP1. 
Annualize Payroll – OpCo, “Rep-Labor Workpapers,” explain why the Company 
believes it is appropriate to reflect a wage increase of 1.5 percent in April and October for 
union TWU-101, when the latest union contract reflects a wage increase of 1.5 only for 
April.

Response: 
 
1. 
Please see the Company’s response to DPS-029 for the latest KEDNY TWU Local 101 
and IBEW Local 3 union contracts supporting the associated wage increases used in the 
Rate Year labor forecast. 
2. 
The KEDNY TWU Local 101 contract expires on October 15, 2019   and given the 
timing, it was reasonable to assume that the new bargained contract would, at a 
minimum, include a 1.5% wage increase for October 2019 as the terms of the recently 
expired contract included wage increases of 1.5% each April and October of 1.5%.  
Therefore, the Company included an assumption of a 1.5% wage increase for October 
2019 in its Rate Year labor forecast.   
Notwithstanding the foregoing, on April 27, 2019 National Grid and TWU Local 101 
negotiated a new three-year contract.  The contract term, which commences on October 
16, 2019 and ends on October 15, 2022, includes a wage increase of 2.75% effective 
October 16, 2019, a 3.0% wage increase effective on October 16, 2020 and a 3.0% wage 
increase effective on October 16, 2021.  Please see Attachment 1 for the latest 
memorandum of agreement between National Grid and TWU Local 101 dated April 27, 
2019.    The increases resulting from this memorandum will be included in the 
Company’s Corrections and Updates filing.

KEYSPAN GAS EAST CORPORATION d/b/a NATIONAL GRID 
THE BROOKLYN UNION GAS COMPANY d/b/a NATIONAL GRID NY 
Case Nos. 19-G-0309 & 19-G-0310 
Gas Utilities Rates 
Request for Information 
FROM: 
DPS Staff, John Castano 
TO: 
National Grid, Gas Infrastructure and Operations Panel (GIOP) 
SUBJECT:
Capitalization Policy Change 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
1.
As stated on pp. 97-98 of KEDNY’s Gas Infrastructure and Operations Panel testimony, 
“[a]ccounting for installation of segments of main under 50 feet in length is currently 
expensed by the Company. This threshold is arbitrary; moreover, there is no similar 
threshold for main replacement in Niagara Mohawk’s service territory. Applicable 
accounting principles and regulations permit capitalization of new main installations, and 
there is no minimum threshold. The Company is proposing to remove the 50-foot 
threshold and capitalize all main installation activities in accordance with the FERC 
Chart of Accounts –Gas – Operating Expense Instructions, Accounts 367 Mains and 376 
Mains. This change will standardize the accounting treatment of these work activities 
between National Grid’s New York gas distribution companies. As discussed in the 
testimony of the Revenue Requirements Panel, the Company has normalized its Historic 
Test Year to reflect the change from expense to capital for distribution and transmission 
main installation, and the Company’s capital investment forecasts also reflect this 
capitalization change.” 
a.
For KEDNY, identify all cost elements in which a normalizing adjustment was 
made to account for the capitalization of installments of main under 50-feet. 
b.
For KEDNY, identify the cost elements in which a normalizing adjustment was 
not made for the capitalization of installments of main under 50-feet, and explain 
why this normalizing adjustment was not warranted. 
Exhibit____(RRP-11CU)
Workpapers to Exhibit RRP-3CU 
Schedule 24
Workpaper 3
Page 1 of 3


--- Page 671 ---
Form 103 
Response: 
 
a.
For KEDNY, all cost elements containing expenses in the HTY associated with 
50 feet or less of main installation were normalized to reflect the Rate Year and 
Data Years change in capitalization policy described in the Gas Infrastructure and 
Operations Panel testimony at pages 97 and 98, with the exception of the 
transportation cost element discussed in Part (b) below.  
Because the Rate Year and Data Years expense in the following cost elements is 
forecast by inflating the normalized HTY expense amount, these cost elements 
have discrete HTY normalization adjustments applied directly in the exhibit 
removing the amount of HTY expense related to the 50 feet or less of main 
installation: 
i. RRP-3, Schedule 2: Contractors 
ii. RRP-3, Schedule 4: Employee Expenses 
iii. RRP-3, Schedule 7: Other 
iv. RRP-3, Schedule 19: Materials-Outside Vendor 
v. RRP-3, Schedule 20: Materials-Inventory 
vi. RRP-3, Schedule 21: Materials-Stores Handling 
vii. RRP-3, Schedule 23: Labor 
The cost elements listed below do not have discrete normalization adjustments 
applied because the Rate Year forecast is not based on HTY expense inflated.  
Instead, the Rate Year and Data Years’ amounts are forecast in total and the 
expense amount determined by applying the labor capitalization rate.  Because 
labor has been normalized for the capitalization policy change (as shown in the 
cost elements list above), the labor capitalization rate based on that labor has been 
normalized.  By applying that labor capitalization rate to the total forecast cost for 
the cost elements below, the resulting expense amount is normalized for the 
capitalization policy change. 
viii. RRP-3, Schedule 11: FAS 106 – OPEB  
ix. RRP-3, Schedule 12: FAS 112 
x. RRP-3, Schedule 13: Healthcare 
xi. RRP-3, Schedule 14: Group Life Insurance 
xii. RRP-3, Schedule 16: Pensions 
xiii. RRP-3, Schedule 17: Thrift Plan 
xiv. RRP-3, Schedule 18: Worker’s Comp 
xv. RRP-3, Schedule 23: Labor (Variable Pay) 
b.
The one cost element that was inadvertently not normalized for the capitalization 
policy change is transportation expense.  The capital and expense ratios of total 
transportation costs in the HTY are applied to the Rate Year and Data Years’ 
forecast of total transportation costs to obtain the expense portion.  Because the 
HTY capital and expense ratios for transportation costs were not normalized for 
Exhibit____(RRP-11CU)
Workpapers to Exhibit RRP-3CU 
Schedule 24
Workpaper 3
Page 2 of 3


--- Page 672 ---
Form 103 
the capitalization policy change, the Rate Year and Data Years’ transportation 
expense has not been normalized.  HTY transportation expense associated with 
the 50 feet or less of main installation is $.068 million for KEDNY.  The 
Company will make this adjustment in its Corrections & Updates filing.

KEYSPAN GAS EAST CORPORATION d/b/a NATIONAL GRID 
THE BROOKLYN UNION GAS COMPANY d/b/a NATIONAL GRID NY 
Case Nos. 19-G-0309 & 19-G-0310 
Gas Utilities Rates 
Request for Information 
FROM: 
DPS Staff, Sarah E. Keymel 
TO: 
National Grid, Revenue Requirements Panel 
SUBJECT:
Other Initiatives - FTEs 
Request: 
Note: In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be 
construed as requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in 
original electronic format with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
1. In the same format as the “Labor Burdens” tab in the MS Excel Format Spreadsheet 
Workpaper, KEDNY Exhibit___(RRP-3), OM Schedule 27, Other Initiatives, provide the 
actual burden rates for each month from 1/1/16 to present.  
2. In the same format as the “Labor Burdens” tab in the MS Excel Format Spreadsheet 
Workpaper, Exhibit___(RRP-3), OM Schedule 27, Other Initiatives, provide the labor burden 
rates using the rate year numbers. 
3. Provide the analyses KEDNY performed to determine that using the adjusted Historic Test 
Year (HTY) amounts to calculate the labor burden rates was reasonable. If no analyses were 
performed, explain why the Company used the HTY amounts. 
Response: 
 
1. See Attachment 1 for the labor overhead rates.  The labor overhead rates presented in 
Attachment 1 are from the Company’s SAP accounting system for the periods indicated. 
2. See Attachment 2 for the labor overhead rates in the Rate Year calculated as the ratio of each 
labor overhead to total base labor. 
3. The Company applied HTY overhead rates to determine Rate Year labor overheads in
